Chapter 6: Cultivating Positive Emotion—The Practice of Gratitude and Savoring
Now that we’ve laid down the basics of strengths and resilience, let’s take the next step together—intentionally nurturing positive emotion in your everyday life.
Have you ever noticed how negative emotions seem to grab your attention, while the good ones just... slip by? Positive feelings can be like sunlight—warming you up for a moment, then gone before you know it. But here’s the thing: research shows that when you make a habit of noticing and amplifying these positive moments, you actually boost your well-being. You open your mind, build up resources for the future, and set yourself up for a richer, more resilient life.
There are two habits that really make a difference here: gratitude and savoring.
Let’s start with gratitude. Imagine making a conscious choice to notice and appreciate the good stuff in your life—no matter how small. It goes way beyond just saying “thank you.” Gratitude is a shift in mindset. Instead of focusing on what’s missing, you start seeing what’s already there. Maybe you jot down three things that went well today, or you write a quick note to someone who made a difference for you. Over time, you train your brain to pick up on kindness, beauty, or even a bit of luck—even on those tough days.
Then there’s savoring. Think of it as the art of stretching out the good moments, letting them last a little longer. Maybe you take an extra minute to enjoy your morning coffee, or you replay a happy memory in your mind. Sometimes, it’s as simple as sharing a joyful moment with someone else. Savoring is like snapping a mental photo—one you can return to any time you need a boost.
Want to bring these habits into your life? Here are a few ideas:
Try gratitude journaling. Each evening, just write down three things you’re grateful for—and, here’s the important part, why they mattered to you.
Create savoring rituals. When something good happens, pause. Take a breath. Really let yourself feel that moment.
And don’t keep the joy to yourself. Share a positive experience with a friend or loved one. Talking about it actually helps the memory stick and deepens your connection.
Remember, this isn’t about ignoring the hard stuff. It’s about giving your mind a break from its usual habit of focusing on problems. Over time, practices like gratitude and savoring help you build up a reservoir of positive emotion—a well you can draw from when you need resilience the most.
So, why not start today? Let those good moments linger, and see how your perspective begins to change.
